story.title: Judge Blocks Trump Administration's Plan to Move FBI Headquarters
story.summary: A U.S. judge has blocked the Trump administration's plans to relocate the FBI headquarters to a federal office building in Washington, D.C. The administration sought to abandon a previously approved site selected under the Biden administration in favor of repurposing another building nearby.

explore_lenses.label: Why does the headquarters fight matter?
explore_lenses.title: The current FBI building has long-standing operational problems
explore_lenses.summary: The dispute is not only about location: the court record describes a headquarters system strained by an aging main building and dispersed personnel. The ruling preserves the prior Greenbelt project for now but does not itself deliver a finished replacement facility.

claims.text: The court found that the J. Edgar Hoover Building has physically deteriorated and cannot meet the FBI's staffing and security needs; it also cited the operational challenges created by headquarters personnel working across multiple National Capital Region locations.

GSA's 2023 rationale for Greenbelt was that it had the lowest projected site-preparation cost, strong rail access, greater schedule certainty, and sustainability and equity advantages among the three congressionally specified sites.

The FBI said the Reagan Building proposal was intended to make government more cost-effective and argued that the court had improperly intervened; Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown said the ruling protects funds Congress had set aside for the Greenbelt project.

explore_lenses.label: How did the dispute reach this point?
explore_lenses.title: A congressionally directed selection was later reversed
explore_lenses.summary: Congress required GSA to choose among three previously identified sites, leading to the 2023 Greenbelt selection. In July 2025, FBI and GSA selected the Ronald Reagan Building and reprogrammed funds; the court held those actions unlawful.

claims.text: Congress directed GSA in 2022 to select an FBI suburban headquarters site from Greenbelt and Landover, Maryland, and Springfield, Virginia; GSA publicly announced Greenbelt as its selection on November 9, 2023.

The August 17, 2026 order vacated the FBI's and GSA's July 2025 selections of the Ronald Reagan Building and the FBI decision to reprogram $555 million for its relocation, renovation, build-out and furnishing.

The court rejected the administration's argument that later congressional actions had ratified or implicitly repealed the earlier site-selection requirements, concluding the Reagan Building decisions were not in accordance with law.

explore_lenses.label: What happens next after the injunction?
explore_lenses.title: The Reagan plan is barred while funding and litigation remain unresolved
explore_lenses.summary: The order permanently bars implementation of the Reagan Building move and requires the parties to report back to the court. Congress's funding conditions and any further statutory action remain material to whether the Greenbelt project proceeds.

claims.text: The permanent injunction bars the defendants from relocating the FBI to the Reagan Building, renovating or furnishing it for FBI use, or reprogramming, obligating, or disbursing funds to support that move.
The parties must file a joint status report within 14 days of the August 17, 2026 order, proposing next steps and stating whether the court may close the case.

The court said the injunction could be revisited if Congress takes statutory action to rescind or alter the site-selection provisions. Separately, the 2026 appropriations law bars further obligation of specified reprogrammed funds until the FBI submits a completed architectural and engineering plan; the court said no such plan had been submitted as of its decision.

story_report.summary: A federal judge has halted the Trump administration’s plan to abandon the previously selected Greenbelt, Maryland, site for a new FBI headquarters and instead move the bureau into Washington’s Ronald Reagan Building. The Aug. 17 order vacated the FBI’s and General Services Administration’s 2025 Reagan Building decisions, including a plan to reprogram $555 million for relocation, renovation, build-out and furnishings. A permanent injunction bars agencies from spending or taking further action to support the proposed move.

sections.heading: Court Rejects Reagan Building Plan
sections.body: The court concluded that the Reagan Building decisions were not in accordance with law. It rejected the administration’s position that subsequent congressional measures had ratified the change or implicitly repealed earlier requirements governing the headquarters site selection. Congress had directed GSA in 2022 to choose among Greenbelt and Landover, Maryland, and Springfield, Virginia; GSA announced Greenbelt as the selected location in November 2023.

sections.heading: Greenbelt Selection and FBI Needs
sections.body: GSA said its 2023 selection of Greenbelt reflected the lowest projected site-preparation cost among the three specified sites, rail access, greater schedule certainty, and sustainability and equity considerations. The court also found that the aging J. Edgar Hoover Building could not meet the FBI’s staffing and security needs, while personnel spread across multiple locations in the National Capital Region created operational difficulties. The FBI said the Reagan Building proposal was intended to make government more cost-effective, while Maryland Attorney General Anthony Brown said the ruling protects funds set aside for Greenbelt.

sections.heading: FBI Headquarters Case Next Steps
sections.body: The parties must submit a joint status report within 14 days of the Aug. 17 order, proposing next steps and stating whether the case can be closed. The court said the injunction could be reconsidered if Congress enacts legislation changing or rescinding the site-selection provisions. Separately, the 2026 appropriations law prevents further obligation of specified reprogrammed funds until the FBI provides a completed architectural and engineering plan; the court said none had been submitted when it ruled.

unresolved.text: The available record does not establish whether the administration will appeal, whether Congress will change the governing site-selection law, or when Greenbelt construction could restart.
The record does not establish when a replacement FBI headquarters will be completed or its final total cost.

related_stories.title: Murder Trial for Tupac Shakur Opens 30 Years After His Death
related_stories.summary: The murder trial for Tupac Shakur has commenced nearly 30 years after the rapper was killed in a drive-by shooting in Las Vegas. Prosecutors allege that a former street gang leader, known as 'Keffe D,' orchestrated the attack as an act of revenge for the beating of his nephew. The trial marks a significant development in a case that has long been considered one of the most prominent cold cases in the U.S.
